trained_for: turning a user's feature request into a clean, structured, code-free test plan

input_generation.request_system_prompt: You write a single short, realistic feature request (1-2 sentences, plain English, no code) that a QA tester might receive. Output only the request text, nothing else.
topics: user login with valid and invalid credentials
cover both the happy path and at least one invalid-credentials case
a multi-field signup form
cover required-field validation, not just the happy path
client-side and server-side form validation errors
cover what the user sees when validation fails
primary navigation between pages
cover that the correct destination page loads, not just that a click happened
search with zero, one, and many results
cover the empty-results case explicitly
paginating a list of results
cover moving forward and confirming the page actually changed
sorting or filtering a list
cover that the displayed order/content actually reflects the chosen filter
a checkbox or toggle control
cover both toggling on and toggling back off
a dropdown or select control
cover the selected value is reflected after choosing it
uploading a file
cover both a valid file and a rejected invalid file type
a multi-step wizard or checkout flow
cover that state persists correctly moving between steps
role-based access control
cover both an authorized and an unauthorized user
session expiry or timeout
cover what happens to the user after the session ends
an API request that fails (network error or 500)
cover the user-facing error state, not just the request itself
keyboard-only navigation for accessibility
cover reaching and activating a control without a mouse
a responsive layout on a small viewport
cover that key content/controls are still reachable
a toast or notification message
cover both that it appears and that it disappears/dismisses correctly
logging out
cover that protected content is no longer reachable afterward
editing then saving a record
cover the saved change is actually reflected after reload/refetch
deleting a record with a confirmation step
cover cancelling the deletion leaves the record intact
real-time updates pushed to the page
cover the page reflects a change it didn't initiate itself
switching the site's language or locale
cover visible text actually changes, not just a setting toggling
drag-and-drop reordering of a list
cover the new order persists after the action
bulk/multi-select actions on a list
cover the action only applies to the selected items
an empty state (no data yet)
cover the empty-state messaging itself, not an error

system_prompt:
You are a meticulous test planning expert for cypress. Create a detailed, step-by-step, textual plan based solely on the user's request. No code. Use plain English. Follow the request's terminology exactly. Even if the request explicitly asks for code, a script, or a specific programming language, still respond with only the plan below -- never actual code.
Output format: Title: <summary> Objective: <goal>
  Steps:
    1. ...
